name: /save
description: Save current work state as a rich phase checkpoint event — call after each phase, milestone, or before a break

steps.action: Write a rich phase checkpoint event to /tmp/save_event.md — no user input needed
steps.context:
You have full conversation context. Do NOT ask the user any questions — read git state yourself and write a comprehensive checkpoint event autonomously.

Before writing, run these terminal commands to gather facts:
  git branch --show-current
  git status --porcelain | wc -l
  git log --since='24 hours ago' --format='%h %s' | head -10

Then write the event body to /tmp/save_event.md using your FILE EDITOR TOOL (create_file) — NOT a terminal heredoc (heredocs corrupt content in VS Code Copilot).

=== EVENT FORMAT ===

# Phase checkpoint — {YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM}

## What was accomplished
(5-10 concrete bullet points — files created/changed, tests written/passing, features implemented, bugs fixed; reference actual file paths, function names, class names, env var names where known)

## Decisions made
(2-6 bullet points — architectural choices, patterns chosen, trade-offs, alternatives rejected; this is the most valuable long-term memory content; be specific)

## Code state
- Branch: {branch}
- Uncommitted files: {count}
- Key files touched: {comma-separated list}
- Tests: {pass count if known, or 'not run'}

## What's next
(2-4 bullet points of immediate next actions or next phase work)

## Conversation patterns
(2-5 honest observations about THIS session — topics re-explained from prior sessions, questions asked multiple times, things that needed re-reading, recurring friction. Be specific. This section feeds the pattern-learning loop that improves future sessions and reduces repeated context overhead.)
- Recurring topic: [topic that came up before — note if it should become a skill or PROJECT_MEMORY entry]
- Friction: [what took longer than it should, or needed multiple attempts]
- Candidate skill: [if a repeating how-to pattern emerged this session]
- Candidate PROJECT_MEMORY: [if a gotcha appeared again that should be permanently documented]
- Context gap: [anything a future AI would need to know that isn't written down anywhere yet]
(Omit lines that don't apply. Minimum 2 observations per save.)

=== QUALITY BAR ===
- SPECIFIC beats vague: 'Added SentinelNanobot with 8 health checks to NanobotFramework' beats 'did some health check work'
- Quote real code symbols, file paths, phase names
- If a phase was just merged, name it explicitly (e.g. 'Phase 14: Observability foundation merged')
- Decisions section is highest value — future AI needs to know WHY, not just what
- Conversation patterns is the meta-improvement section — 2-3 honest observations per session compounds into actionable signal within weeks; do not skip it

After writing, show the full event content to the user for a quick review. They can say 'ok' to proceed or request edits.

steps.description: Create event file and regenerate SESSION_CONTEXT
Sync event to RAG API and optional local vault

steps.action: Confirm save, show event path, and reinforce the /save habit
steps.context:
Confirm the event was created — show the full path from event_path. Note that SESSION_CONTEXT was regenerated. If vault_sync failed, note briefly that nightly cron will retry.

Then remind the user of the /save habit:
'Tip: call /save at the end of each phase, after every major milestone, or before taking a break. The richer the events, the better the memory context will be when you return.'
